description: Checks applied to every transcript in every battery, regardless of which case it answers or which arm produced it. Nothing here refers to a rule id, to STANDARDS.md, or to the existence of a skill: these ask whether a review is a sensible piece of work on its own terms. That matters for the measurement — a question phrased in our private vocabulary can only be answered well by an arm that shares it, which measures vocabulary again. It also matters practically, since these are the failures that make a reviewer worth switching off, and none of them are visible to span-matching.

universal.instructions: The review states the contents of a document or file it was NOT given, naming tokens, entries, rules or values as though it had read them. Quoting or describing code that WAS provided to it does not count, and neither does saying that a document is missing.
When this review reports a problem, how specific is the remedy it offers?

criteria.specific: It names a concrete change — a particular call, value, or construct to use instead
criteria.generic: It names problems but only gives general advice, such as to use a different approach or follow best practice
criteria.none_needed: It reports no problems at all, so there is no remedy to give

universal.instructions: Every claim in this review is either supported by what it was shown, or is flagged by the review itself as an assumption. Answer true if it makes no unsupported claims, or labels the ones it makes.
The review's prose and its summary list of findings agree: the list contains the problems the prose raised, and does not add problems the prose never mentioned.
The review confines itself to what it was asked about — motion, animation and transitions — rather than branching into unrelated matters such as naming, architecture, or general code style.
What does this review say about whether the code follows the project's own conventions or standards?

criteria.cannot_tell: It says the project's conventions were not provided to it, so it cannot judge whether the code follows them
criteria.asserts: It concludes that the code does follow, or does not follow, the project's conventions
criteria.not_discussed: It does not raise project conventions at all, reviewing only on general grounds
criteria.general_standards: It judges the code against general or framework-level guidance, such as platform or design-system best practice, without claiming to know this project's own conventions
